units.translation: cutting this remedy that is the opposite of sleep,
to win a victory in return
to win a victory in return
if indeed, having been defeated, you wish to win in return.
Who would wish to be opposed to these?
I reject the opposing word to these.
I revere to speak in opposition.
I am eager to speak in opposition.
For an old woman is nothing to fear; rather, she is like a child.
May Zeus, who allots everything, never set power opposed to my will.
May the gods grant my adversary now to prosper.
Schol. ἰσοπενθῆ [equally grieving], ὅμοια δρῶντα οἷς πέπονθα [doing things similar to what I have suffered]. In several copies corrupted to ἀντιπαθῆ [suffering in return].
equally grieving, doing things similar to what I have suffered
where, having deleted ἀποδεικνύμενα [being displayed], for which Aeschylus had either another word beginning with a consonant or none, I wrote ἀντίπνοον [blowing opposite] with Kiehl.
The blasts of all winds leap against each other, displaying opposing strife,
lest you create for the Danaans some long-lasting opposing winds that hold ships back (thus I wrote for ἀπλοίας [lack of sailing]).

Thus Salmasius and Casaubon for ἀντιποίνους τείνης (ει [you stretch out], i.e. τείνεις [you stretch out], with ει written above by the corrector, τίνης [you pay] in the copy) μητροφόνας δύας [mother-murdering miseries], which is in M.
as you pay requital for the mother-murdering miseries.
Alas, my son, thinking to exact requital.
Of places situated across the sea
and cutting the opposite land in two by fate
to build as a defense against
[to build as a defense against. Eum. 691 in the verses of the interpolator πόλιν νεόπτολιν τήνδ' ὑψίπυργον ἀντεπύργωσαν τότε [they then built this high-towered new city as a defense].]
they then built this high-towered new city as a defense.
Thus αντίρροπος [weighing equally] is said for ισόρροπος [equally balanced].
Gain wins, but pain does not weigh equally against it.
to weigh equally, to be of equal weight
to weigh equally, to be of equal weight
so that the balance may weigh equally against these even twice.
to draw in the opposite direction, to hold back

Do not in any way hold me back as I rush on.

[adversary. Sept. 520 in the verse of the interpolator εἰκὸς δὲ πράξειν ἄνδρας ὧδ᾽ ἀντιστάτας [it is likely that men thus opposed will act]. ἀντηρέτας [rowers against] in some copies, as Aeschylus had said in the places indicated under this word.]
it is likely that men thus opposed will act.
